meta.title: Which laptop should I buy?
meta.subtitle: Comparing three options under $1,600 for a mix of coding and travel
meta.description: Four criteria matter most: price, how well it handles a dev workload, battery life away from a desk, and how easy repairs/upgrades are down the line.

criteria.label: Price
criteria.description: 10 = cheapest of the three, 1 = most expensive.

criteria.label: Dev workload performance
criteria.description: 10 = fastest for compiling/running containers/multiple VMs, based on published multi-core benchmark scores.

criteria.label: Battery life away from a charger
criteria.description: 10 = longest manufacturer-rated battery life among the three.

criteria.label: Repairability / upgradeability
criteria.description: 10 = RAM and storage are user-replaceable with widely available parts; 1 = fully soldered, no official repair program.

criteria.label: Screen quality
criteria.description: 10 = best measured color accuracy and brightness among the three in independent reviews.

frameworkDiy.price: DIY edition starts around $1,000 fully specced closer to $1,350 — mid-pack, not the cheapest once RAM/SSD are added.
frameworkDiy.performance: 13th-gen Core i5/i7 options land mid-pack on multi-core benchmarks versus the other two — solid but not class-leading.
frameworkDiy.battery: Manufacturer-rated ~8-10h mixed use; shortest of the three, partly the tradeoff for modularity.
frameworkDiy.repairability: Modular mainboard, user-replaceable RAM/SSD/battery/ports, official repair guides and spare parts store — best in class by design intent.
frameworkDiy.screen: 2.8K 120Hz panel is good but independent reviews rate color accuracy and peak brightness below the MacBook Air.

macbookAir.price: 15-inch M3 starts at $1,299, cheapest entry point of the three for a comparably specced machine.
macbookAir.performance: M3's multi-core benchmark scores lead both Windows options comfortably at this price and this is a fanless chassis, so it's also silent under load.
macbookAir.battery: Apple rates up to 18h video playback; independent real-world tests still show it comfortably ahead of the other two.
macbookAir.repairability: Soldered RAM and storage, no official self-repair parts for this model — weakest of the three on this criterion.
macbookAir.screen: Liquid Retina display rated highest of the three for color accuracy and brightness in independent reviews.

thinkpadT14.price: List price runs higher, but business discounts/sales commonly bring it to the cheapest effective price of the three — scored on typical street price, not list.
thinkpadT14.performance: Ryzen/Core mobile chips here benchmark above the Framework DIY config but below the M3 on multi-core workloads.
thinkpadT14.battery: Rated ~9-11h; middle of the pack, slightly ahead of the Framework DIY unit.
thinkpadT14.repairability: ThinkPads keep user-accessible RAM/SSD bays and Lenovo publishes official repair manuals — very good, just short of Framework's fully modular design.
thinkpadT14.screen: Business-panel options are functional but reviews consistently rate color accuracy and brightness lowest of the three.
